text:
erin: quick heads-up: sampleapp users reporting long tail latency—short auth requests get queued behind long streaming calls. suspect OkHttp Dispatcher + HTTP/2 multiplexing oddness on some OEMs.

sam: interesting. what's the client config?

erin: default builder, but we changed Dispatcher to maxRequests=32, maxRequestsPerHost=8 and connectionPool(10,5m). streams are HTTP/2. when one stream stalls (socket stalled by OEM power mgmt), other inbound auth requests pile up. logs: 
```
D/OkHttp: queued request (maxRequestsPerHost reached)
D/OkHttp: running request /v1/generate (streaming)
D/OkHttp: running request /v1/auth/refresh (waiting)
```
erin: result: token refresh delayed -> 401 cascades -> retry floods.

kai: I've seen this. HTTP/2 multiplexing doesn't protect you when the single TCP connection is blocked; Dispatcher counts active calls and blocks new ones because maxRequestsPerHost counts streams across the connection.

sam: mitigation options: 1) split auth traffic to a separate host or tag and use a second client with its own connection pool/dispatcher; 2) mark auth calls with `tag()` and use custom Dispatcher that prioritizes short calls; 3) lower maxRequestsPerHost and rely on intelligent batching.

erin: second client seems easiest. we can create a tiny `authOkHttpClient` with small pool and keepalive to avoid being head-of-line blocked by streaming.

kai: also consider enabling `pingInterval` for long-lived connections to detect half-closed sockets faster. For OEMs that buffer TCP, that helps.

sam: can we add a note in onboarding: "If you use streaming endpoints, create a separate OkHttp client for auth to avoid head-of-line blocking"? include sample code.

erin: will draft a small PR: separate auth client + sampleapp change + test matrix (Pixel 5/6, Android 12-14, OEM variants).

ops-bot: Issue created: DEX-5150 "Android: HTTP/2 multiplexing + Dispatcher head-of-line blocking causes queued auth requests" (<https://issues.redwood/DEX-5150>)

erin: thanks — will attach minimal repro and perf traces.
